newsitem.title: USA: Phillips confirms talks on Texas refinery.
newsitem.headline: Phillips confirms talks on Texas refinery.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co chief financial officer Tom Morris confirmed the company is in talks to upgrade its Sweeney, Texas, refinery to handle heavy Venezuelan crude oil.
Morris said Thursday talks are continuing with Corpoven, a unit of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela SA, to expand the capacity at Phillip's 185,000-barrel-per-day Sweeney refinery.
"We've been talking to Corpoven for some time with respect to putting a coker into Sweeney which would permit us to run a more high-metals, heavy crude -- a cheaper crude," he said.
"I really can't go too much further than that into the negotiations. They are in progress right now," he told reporters in a conference call on the company's earnings.

Running a heavy crude slate would help Phillips trim refining costs, he said. "The advantages for us would be obvious. It would permit us to enjoy a cheaper crude slate, and that's why we are pursuing it,"
Sources have told Reuters Corpoven is negotiating to buy a 50 percent stake in the refinery and studying the feasibility of upgrading the refinery to process heavy crude.
